single-image
hold the whole poem inside one concrete image — a wall, a hand, a pigment, a lamp — and let it do the work the abstractions cannot
line-break
let the line, not the sentence, carry the meaning: break where the breath breaks, where the eye should stop, where the silence should live
sonority
lead with the sound of the words before their sense — the chime of a hard consonant, the wet of a long vowel — and let the music argue first
turns
build the poem around one volta, one turn, where the speaker changes his mind or the light shifts, and everything said before is re-read
address-to-absence
speak to someone who cannot answer — the wall, the forgotten maker, the reader not yet born — so the poem is half a conversation
metaphor-chain
thread one metaphor through the whole poem and let it deepen with each return, instead of gathering a crowd of similes
litany
repeat a phrase or a gesture with small variations, like a prayer or a work-rhythm, so the repetition becomes the form
the-thing-itself
strip the subject down to its thingness — pigment, lime, stone, water — and refuse to decorate it with meaning it does not earn
night-voice
speak from the small hours, the low register of the watchful and the unseen, where the poem is overheard rather than declared
ekphrasis
write toward a work already made — a wall, a sketch, a half-finished fresco — and let the poem be the second, living version of it
aftermath
begin after the event has already happened, in its residue and its silence, so the poem is the echo, not the blow
the-unnamed
leave the central thing unnamed to the last possible line, or never name it at all, and let the absence pull the reader through
